J1.evidence: The reviewer's omission claim is wrong: the EN does contain the whole Rhetoric/al-taʿrīḍ section. But the EN has a real meaning error there: Arabic «وإنما قصد تقريره لنفسه، وإثباته لها» (لها = نفسه, i.e. himself) is rendered 'to establish it for himself and affirm it for them'; it must be 'affirm it for himself'. Also the source's «أأنت كتب هذا؟» (misprint for كتبت) is silently corrected to 'Did you write this?' without the required [Translator's note] (TR flags it). Needs a fix.

J2.evidence: The claimed omission is not real: the stored English contains the whole Rhetoric (التعريض) section through «لا نفية عنك وإثباته للأميّ أو المخربش». But the reading has a wrong-meaning error there: «وإنما قصد تقريره لنفسه، وإثباته لها» means 'he intended to establish it for himself and affirm it for himself (لها = نفسه)', whereas the English says 'establish it for himself and affirm it for them', assigning the affirmation to the idolaters. Needs fixing to 'affirm it for himself'.
